paragraphs: Edit distance appears throughout software systems wherever identifiers, source code, package names, domains, logs, or event sequences must be compared under small structural changes. In security, a one-character insertion, deletion, substitution, or Unicode lookalike can distinguish a legitimate identifier from a typosquatting or supply-chain attack; in software analysis, textual edit distance can provide a useful baseline for comparing source code but must be separated from syntax-aware AST similarity and semantic program equivalence; and in operational systems, edit distance can compare ordered logs or event traces when missing, added, or changed events matter. This section examines these applications while maintaining a critical boundary: small string distance can indicate structural resemblance, but it does not by itself establish common authorship, malicious intent, software equivalence, or real-world identity.

01 Log and Event-Sequence Similarity: Edit Distance, Trace Alignment, Anomaly Detection, and Observability A rigorous guide to log and event-sequence similarity, covering event parsing, sessionization, Levenshtein alignment, weighted costs, LCS, temporal distance, process traces, anomaly detection, security events, scalable retrieval, and failure modes. Article · 24 min read

02 Typosquatting and Software Supply-Chain Security: Edit Distance, Package Impersonation, Detection, and Defense A rigorous guide to typosquatting and software supply-chain security, covering edit-distance detection, package impersonation, Unicode confusables, dependency confusion, slopsquatting, false positives, behavioral analysis, and layered defenses. Article · 11 min read

03 Unicode Homoglyph and Confusable Attacks: Edit Distance, UTS #39, IDN Spoofing, and Defense A technical guide to Unicode homoglyph and confusable attacks, UTS #39, confusable skeletons, mixed-script spoofing, IDN security, and the role of Levenshtein distance in detecting deceptive identifiers. Article · 11 min read

04 Source Code and AST Similarity: Edit Distance, Clone Detection, Tree Differencing, and Semantic Limits A rigorous guide to source-code similarity, covering text and token edit distance, code-clone types, AST similarity, tree edit distance, GumTree, Deckard, NiCad, SourcererCC, semantic clones, benchmarks, and limitations. Article · 46 min read
